titre: Hitchhiking through Mayenne, penniless, with our bosses
description: Portraits 2 Passages takes you to Mayenne — the department, the town and the river!
chapo: Portraits 2 Passages takes you to Mayenne — the department, the town and the river!
corps: On the programme: two 100% unlikely duos — Nicolas & Jean-François (his boss) and Diane & Gwenola (her manager) — taking on challenges cooked up by Lou. Will they still be getting along at work once the adventure is over?
defis: Head to the highest point of the Armorican Massif to see a mural. Can you find out which artist painted it? Ask around!
Mont des Avaloirs, at 416 m. The artist is Seb Toussaint.
William II besieged me and ended up setting me on fire. Barons later put me back on my feet, but I no longer welcomed kings — I was more the type to welcome prisoners.
My life was complicated: caught up in the Vendée wars, I was denounced and guillotined on 5 March 1794. Today my grave lies in the middle of the fields — good luck finding me!
I am a unique natural site in Mayenne, known for my impressive rock formations and my legends.
I stand right next to Suzanne, but between you and me, passers-by only have eyes for me.
I was built in 1096 in Haut-Anjou. I saw canons regular walk through my naves, and part of me collapsed in 1795. But which part?
I was born thanks to textiles during the 19th century. Find someone who can tell you the history of this place!

I am a haven of peace and greenery, perched above the calm waters of the Mayenne. I used to be a private garden, but today I stretch over 4.5 hectares for everyone to enjoy. I also keep the memory of two famous children of this land: a painter and a sailor.
Which town does this coat of arms belong to? What does it represent? And what is the story behind these symbols? Go to the town in question to answer these questions.

Ernée. The story behind these whistles (or “subious”) is uncertain. One version goes like this: the townspeople hid when the English invaded, and when three whistle blasts rang out, they burst out of their hiding places and chased away the surprised English.
I am a place where religion and the arts meet. My theatre can seat up to 500 people! Visit my gardens to enjoy the serenity of the place.
The Virgin appeared here on 17 January 1871. Since then, I have been a Marian town.
